bio: Mai Yang Vang (born 1984 or 1985) is an American politician who has served on the Sacramento, California, City Council since 2020. A member of the Democratic Party, she represents the 8th district and is the first Asian-American woman and first person of Hmong descent elected to the body.

items.t: Co-led the effort to pass the first Safe Haven resolution in the Sacramento City Unified School District.
items.q: She co-led the effort to pass the first ever Safe Haven resolution in SCUSD

items.t: Is running for Congress in part because she is against increased Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity in the region.
items.q: Her decision to run was motivated by her opposition to the increase in Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity in the region.

items.t: Helped pass Ethnic Studies as a high school graduation requirement in Sacramento City Unified School District.
items.q: was instrumental in passing Ethnic Studies as a high school requirement.

items.t: Co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics to mobilize residents and parents against school closures in South Sacramento (2013).
items.q: In 2013, Vang co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics to organize the South Sacramento Hmong community, register voters, and mobilize residents and parents against school closures

items.t: Voted to shift $6 million from Sacramento police overtime and unfilled vacancies to expand hours of the homeless behavioral health department (2023).
items.q: In 2023, Vang voted to shift $6 million away from the Sacramento City police overtime and unfilled vacancies, and reallocate the money into expanding the hours of the homeless behavioral health department

items.t: Was the only council member to vote against renewing ShotSpotter detection technology.
items.q: Vang was the only council member to vote against the renewal of the controversial ShotSpotter detection technology.

items.t: As a school board member, raised concerns about the presence of police officers on school grounds.
items.q: consistently raised concerns about the presence of police officers on school grounds.

items.t: Highlighted affordable housing as a priority in her 2020 city council campaign.
items.q: Vang highlighted affordable housing, public health, and her district becoming integral in the farm to fork movement.

items.t: Led the effort to secure the city's first citywide language access coordinator.
items.q: Vang lead the effort to secure the first-ever city-wide language access coordinator to make sure government was accessible to everyday people.

items.t: Worked to secure funding for city library services through Measure E (2024).
items.q: Vang and Vice Mayor Karina Talamantes worked with the community to support and secure funding for city library services through Measure E.

items.t: During her tenure, Sacramento established the first Children's Fund, dedicating $10 million annually to children and youth impacted by poverty, violence and trauma.
items.q: the city established the first-ever Sacramento Children’s Fund, dedicating $10 million annually to support children and youth impacted by poverty, violence, and trauma.
